citations.title: Chapter 02 Administrative Requirements for Licensees (.01-1 through .14)
citations.requirement: Chapter table of contents fetched. It lists .01 Incorporation by Reference, .01-1 License Required, .02 Application, .03 Investigation, .04 Compliance Monitoring, .05 New Site/Closure/Relocation, .06 Licensed Capacity, .07 IFC, .08 Governing Body, .09 PSP, .10 Policies and Procedures, .11 Staffing, .12 Health and Safety, .13 Records, .14 Quality Assurance. Authority: Health-General §§7-904 and 7-909.

citations.title: License Required
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide community residential services. Taken from the fact-checked research; the text was not re-fetched.

citations.title: Application for Initial License or Renewal
citations.requirement: A.(1): the licensee must be a Maryland corporation, or a foreign corporation registered in MD. A.(2)-(3): the governing body is legally responsible for overseeing all programs and for compliance. A.(4): the application needs a business plan, a DD experience summary, prior licensing reports from the last 10 years, and a DDA-approved QA plan. B.: file renewal at least 60 days before the license expires. D.: the Director may approve, approve with conditions, deny, or request more information. F.: voluntary surrender needs a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead and approved by the Director. G.: terminate services to an individual only for good cause with the Director's written approval. Give the Director 90 days' written notice, give the individual and proponent written notice of the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, and copy the regional office and team. Services are considered terminated after 60 consecutive days' absence unless the Director decides otherwise.

citations.title: Investigation by the Administration
citations.requirement: Sets OHCQ investigation priorities. Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days. Taken from the fact-checked research. NOTE: the fetched text of .04E, not .03, contains the 10-working-day plan-of-correction rule; cite .04E for the POC deadline.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: A.: OHCQ, as the Administration's agent, monitors and inspects licensees. B.: an on-site pre-licensure survey is required. C.: announced and unannounced licensure visits happen at least annually. D.: announced or unannounced complaint investigation visits. E.: submit a plan of correction (POC) at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving the findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and the OHCQ Director may grant an extension of up to 30 days. F.: if a POC is unacceptable, resubmit a revised POC within 10 working days.

citations.title: New Site, Site Closure, or Relocation
citations.requirement: DDA approval is required at least 30 days in advance to open, close or relocate a site. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Licensed Capacity
citations.requirement: The license states the number of people that may be served. Exceeding it requires Director approval, for a maximum of 60 days plus one 60-day extension. Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Governing Body
citations.requirement: Board membership must include at least 1 person with a DD, 1 family member of a person with a DD, and 1 person with DD experience. At least 75% of members must live in MD or within 100 miles. No employees or their immediate family may be voting members. Bylaws must cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict of interest, POC responses and PSP approval. Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)). Taken from the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Program Service Plan (PSP)
citations.requirement: A.: a PSP is required for each service the licensee provides. B.: submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing changes. C.: the administrative head ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years. D.: comply with the approved PSP. E.: contents are rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location (including the number of individuals expected to be served).

citations.title: Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: A.(1)-(19) requires written policies on: health and safety per the IP; fundamental rights (Health-General §7-1002); promoting choice; confidentiality (Health-General §7-1010); a grievance process with anti-retaliation safeguards; nondiscrimination; reporting and investigating all incidents under DDA procedures; medication administration per DDA's curriculum; compliance with COMAR 10.27.11; behavior safeguards; property-damage payment; Health-General §5-605; no conflict of interest; GAAP fiscal practices; protection of individuals' finances (A(15)(a)-(e)); infection control and standard precautions; a disaster and evacuation plan with sufficient drills; and no individual performing paid staff duties or non-household tasks (A(18)-(19)). B.: group homes need an emergency plan covering evacuation or 72-hour shelter-in-place, an annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners, an after-action report and improvement plan, ID with health information, family and DDA regional office notification, staff recall, continuity of operations, off-site data backup, sharing the plan with local emergency management, and an executive summary for families on request. C.: all staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must know and implement every policy. D.: give each individual and proponent enough information about the grievance process to use it.

citations.title: Staffing Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: analyze the number of individuals and each person's needs, then develop and implement a staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and delivers the IP services. There is no fixed numeric ratio. B.: no employing or contracting with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals (Health-General §19-1902 et seq.; COMAR 12.15.03). C.: before independent duties, staff need job training, DDA-approved training (seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, aging) and OSHA blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030. D.: within 3 months of hire, DDA-approved training on community integration, individual-directed planning, characteristics and needs, First Aid/CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent), fundamental rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice, and communication skills. E.: written job descriptions and a policy to prevent employment discrimination.

citations.title: Health and Safety Requirements
citations.requirement: A.: each home must meet local zoning (except as provided in Health-General §7-603), local and State building codes and life-safety requirements, be free of hazards, and be in good repair. B.: free of fire hazards, with adequate smoke detectors, working and updated fire extinguishers, and a written fire evacuation plan. C.: water temperature at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and this is documented in each IP. D.: administer medication per DDA's medication curriculum, use unit-dose packaging for oral solids unless the IP says otherwise, package medication for absent individuals separately, and request pharmacy-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms.

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: A.: keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served. B.: minimum contents are application identifying information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies, medication list, the IP (COMAR 10.22.05), documentation of IP implementation, and anything else DDA requires. C.: on a medical emergency, make the person's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel. D.: keep records at least 6 years, even if the person leaves or dies. Keep current-service documents for as long as the person is served, and organize records for easy access. E.: electronic records must meet the chapter, comply with HIPAA privacy and security rules, and be backed up and stored off-site.

citations.title: Quality Assurance
citations.requirement: A.: submit the QA plan and any substantive changes to DDA for approval. B.: an internal QA system that is focused on individual choice, preference and satisfaction (with personal contact), has measurable outcomes, analyzes trends, responds promptly when health or safety is at risk, and tracks behavior-plan restrictive techniques (who, which technique, date/time, emergency vs. plan, effectiveness). C.: set goals and standards, keep records, and implement changes based on the data. E.: standing committee(s) must review the incident protocol and all incidents, approve all behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, review and set time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and review policies for protection of rights. The committee must have equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees (individuals, proponents or community members). Members may not decide on incidents or behavior plans they were involved in. It meets as needed with a majority present and must ensure confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010.

citations.title: Scope (Community Residential Services)
citations.requirement: Defines the scope of community residential services (alternative living units, group homes, IFC, CSLA; respite limits). Taken from the fact-checked research; the text was not re-fetched.

citations.title: Staffing and Training (Community Residential Services)
citations.requirement: A.: provide staffing levels and patterns as determined in the IP. B.: provide or arrange training in accordance with COMAR 10.22.02.11.

citations.title: Fundamental Rights
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 04 table of contents (Values, Outcomes, and Fundamental Rights). Rule text was not read. .14E(1)(d)-(e) cross-references .03A for restrictions of rights and for behavior plans that use restrictive techniques. Read .03 before finalizing the rights policy text.

citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents. Rule text was not read.

citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents. Rule text was not read. .14E(1)(d) requires standing-committee approval of behavior plans that use restrictive techniques under 10.22.10.

citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed from the Chapter 10 table of contents and the .14 cross-reference. Rule text was not read.

citations.title: Informal Hearings Under the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Law
citations.requirement: Chapter title confirmed from the link in .02G. Individuals have a right to a hearing under this chapter when services are to be terminated (.02G(2)). Chapter text was not read.

citations.title: Delegation of Nursing Functions
citations.requirement: Chapter title confirmed from the link in .10A(9). The licensee must have a policy ensuring compliance with this chapter. Chapter text was not read.

citations.requirement: Cited in .11B together with Health-General §19-1902 et seq. as the basis for criminal history checks. Chapter text was not read.

citations.title: Criminal history records check (as cited in COMAR 10.22.02.11B)
citations.requirement: COMAR 10.22.02.11B cites §19-1902 et seq. The fact-checked research cites '§19-1901 et seq.'. Confirm the exact starting section against the statute before finalizing. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.requirement: COMAR requires the licensee to have a policy ensuring fundamental rights in accordance with this section. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.title: Confidentiality (as cited in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(4) and .14E(7))
citations.requirement: COMAR requires the licensee to have a confidentiality policy in accordance with this section. The standing committee must also keep confidentiality under it. Statute text was not fetched.

citations.title: Reporting of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult
citations.requirement: Not in the fact-checked research and not fetched. Cited from general knowledge of Maryland's adult abuse reporting law. VERIFY before use. The DDA incident policy and local APS procedures control the details.

citations.cite: DDA Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations (PORII)
citations.title: DDA reportable incident procedures
citations.requirement: COMAR 10.22.02.10A(7) requires incidents to be reported and investigated 'in accordance with the Administration's procedures on reportable incidents'. The current PORII was not fetched, so incident levels, deadlines and forms must be copied from the current DDA PORII before finalizing.

citations.cite: Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C — Community Living – Group Home
citations.title: Service definition, residence requirements, provider standards
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S8). Maximum 4 participants per residence unless previously approved by DDA, with private bedrooms. Services available 24/7 with back-up and emergency support. Staff are 18+ with First Aid/CPR and an in-person skills check. Medication Technician certification (Board of Nursing) for unlicensed staff who give medication. RN delegation. Transportation is included in the daily rate. Room and board are collected from the resident. Retainer days are up to 18 per person per year. No payment to relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons. Provider needs 5 years of DD residential experience.

citations.title: Financial accountability
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S9). Bill only services authorized in the approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization in LTSSMaryland. Room and board are excluded from the rate. EVV is required for Personal Supports and Respite, not for CL–GH.

citations.title: HCBS settings requirements
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S52). Provider-owned or controlled residential settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, privacy, lockable doors, roommate choice, and access to food and visitors.

citations.title: Additional requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings
citations.requirement: Cited in the fact-checked research checklist for lockable bedroom doors and resident control of space. Any modification of these conditions must be supported by a specific assessed need and documented in the person-centered plan.

citations.title: Bloodborne pathogens (OSHA)
citations.requirement: Incorporated by reference in COMAR 10.22.02.11C(3). All staff and care providers must be trained in blood-borne pathogens in accordance with OSHA guidelines before independent duties.

citations.title: Earned sick and safe leave
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S40). Employees accrue 1 hour per 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours per year. Leave is paid when the employer has 15 or more employees.

citations.cite: Maryland Wage and Hour Law facts (MD Labor)
citations.title: State and local minimum wage
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S39). State minimum is $15.00/hr. Montgomery County is $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50 employees, and certain nonprofit and Medicaid-funded home care providers) and $15.95 (10 or fewer). Howard County is $16.00 and Prince George's County is $15.30 (as of July 1, 2026).

citations.cite: DDA Addendum for Participation in Maryland Medical Assistance Program — PT 90 DDA
citations.title: Separate MA number per licensed site
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S30). Each licensed site needs its own 'DDA Licensed Site MA' number. Medicaid enrollment, revalidation and SDAT good-standing checks run through MPRIME (PT 36-27); losing SDAT good standing causes immediate suspension.

citations.cite: Provider Portal Residential Services 2023 Billing Update (Jan 27, 2023)
citations.title: Number of People Authorized / retainer days
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S62). 'Number of People Authorized' (people living in the home and present, or on retainer days, max 18 per year) drives the residential billing rate. Example: when a resident leaves a 4-person home, the other three move from $403.30 to $355.23 per day.

citations.title: Staff Training Form — Developmental Disabilities Services
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S61). DDA form for documenting the COMAR 10.22.02.11C and D training topics.

citations.cite: DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites (MDH Form DD.ADD.1.0, 06.02.2022)
citations.title: Site addendum with Community Settings Rule attestation
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S59). Lists each site, capacity requested and proposed occupancy date, and includes the Community Settings Rule attestation. Also asks whether the site is wheelchair accessible.

citations.cite: DDA New Site Visit Checklist (Community Settings Rule), Nov 14, 2022
citations.title: New site inspection form
citations.requirement: Taken from the fact-checked research (S60). Covers institutional or isolating characteristics, heightened scrutiny (including proximity to the provider's other sites) and settings-rule items.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Program Director Responsibilities
state_specifics: The licensee must be a Maryland corporation, or a registered foreign corporation (.02A(1)). Archived OHCQ guidance says DDA does not accept LLCs.
The governing body is legally responsible for oversight of all programs and for compliance with COMAR 10.22.02 (.02A(2)-(3)).

Board composition: at least 1 person with a DD, 1 family member of a person with a DD, and 1 person with DD experience. At least 75% live in MD or within 100 miles. No employees or immediate family as voting members.
Bylaws cover oversight, compliance, mission/budget/policy approval, conflict-of-interest rules, POC responses and PSP approval.
Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)).
The administrative head or two officers sign license applications and renewals (.02C).
The program director ensures every staff member, care provider, consultant and volunteer knows and implements each policy (.10C).
Managers must have 5+ years of DD experience, per the DDA application.

policies.title: Licensure, Qualified Provider Approval and Medicaid Provider Agreements
state_specifics: Three linked approvals: DDA qualified-provider approval, an OHCQ-administered COMAR 10.22.02 license, and a separate Medicaid MA number for each licensed site (PT 90 DDA addendum).
Provider standard: minimum 5 years of demonstrated DD residential experience.
File the license renewal at least 60 days before expiration (.02B). The license does not expire until the Director acts and judicial review time lapses.
The Director may approve, approve with conditions, deny or request more information (.02D). Denial notice carries a right to a hearing request to OAH within 30 days (.02E).
Keep SDAT good standing and licenses current in MPRIME (PT 36-27; loss of good standing means Medicaid suspension).
Policies and procedures go to OHCQ within 30 days of DDA approval (DDA application §VII.A).
Keep the signed Provider Agreement to Conditions of Participation on file.
Screen owners and managers against the OIG LEIE and the Maryland sanctioned provider list.

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Staff Awareness
state_specifics: Written policies must cover every topic in COMAR 10.22.02.10A(1)-(19) and the .10B emergency plan.
All staff, care providers, consultants and volunteers must be aware of the policies and implement them as adopted (.10C).
The standing committee reviews policies and their implementation to ensure legal and human rights are protected (.14E(1)(f)).
Include a cross-reference table of each COMAR .10A item to the policy ID that covers it.
Policy approval is a governing-body duty under the bylaws (.08C).

policies.title: Quality Assurance Plan, Data Review and Mortality Review
state_specifics: The QA plan, and any substantive changes, require DDA approval (.14A).
The QA system must include personal contact with the people served and track their choices, preferences and satisfaction (.14B(1)).
Goals and standards must be measurable, with records kept to show effectiveness, and changes implemented from the data (.14C). DDA can request documentation to verify goals are being met (.14D).
Track behavior-plan restrictive techniques: individual, medication or technique, date and time, emergency vs. plan, and effectiveness (.14B(4)).
Mortality review: conduct a review of every death through the QA committee. Follow the DDA incident policy (PORII) and any DDA mortality review process, whose current details were not verified here.

policies.title: Standing Committee (Human Rights / Quality Assurance / Incident Review)
state_specifics: Required committee functions: perform QA functions, review the incident protocol, review all incidents, approve behavior plans that use restrictive techniques, review and set time frames for rights restrictions not related to challenging behavior, and review policies (.14E(1)).
Membership must have equal numbers of licensee staff and non-employees (individuals, proponents or community members). A member paid only for committee service counts as neither (.14E(3)).
A member may not take part in decisions on incidents they were involved in or behavior plans they developed (.14E(5)).
The committee meets as needed with at least a majority present (.14E(6)). Keep minutes.
The committee may consult a psychologist, physician, PA, NP or board-certified clinical pharmacist (.14E(4)).
Maintain confidentiality under Health-General §7-1010 (.14E(7)).

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing, Retainer Days and Service Documentation
state_specifics: Bill W5600 Community Living – Group Home per person per day in LTSSMaryland. Bill only services in the approved PCP and Detailed Service Authorization.

Enter 'Number of People Authorized' correctly on every claim. It counts residents living in the home and present, or on a retainer day. A move-out drops the others to the smaller-home rate (4 to 3: $403.30 to $355.23 at the Oct 1, 2026 standard rate).
Retainer days: up to 18 per resident per calendar year for hospitalization, behavioral respite, or family/friend visits.
Room and board are never billed to Medicaid; collect them from the resident under a written agreement.

Dedicated 1:1 hours (W1999) may be shared only in the situations the waiver permits (retired, transitioning, recovering, or few day-service hours). Document in each PCP and bill for one participant only. The threshold is under 40 hours in the current text and under 30 under pending Amendment #4.
Do not pay relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons for CL–GH.
EVV is not required for CL–GH (it applies to Personal Supports and Respite).
The 2% FY2027 rate reduction is pending CMS approval; rates stay at June 30, 2026 levels until then.
Daily documentation must support each billed day. Keep billing records at least 6 years.

policies.title: Program Service Plan Maintenance and DDA Approval of Changes
state_specifics: A PSP is required for each service provided (.09A).
Submit a revised PSP for DDA approval before implementing any change (.09B).
The administrative head ensures the governing body reviews and updates the PSP at least every 3 years (.09C).
Comply with all provisions of the approved PSP (.09D).
The PSP contains rationale, scope, staffing and training, and setting and location, including the number of individuals expected per home (.09E).
An alternative model needs DDA approval through an innovative PSP variance (.09F).

policies.title: Licensed Capacity, New Site, Relocation and Closure
state_specifics: DDA approval is required at least 30 days before opening, closing or relocating any site (.05).
The license states capacity. Exceeding it needs Director approval for up to 60 days, plus one 60-day extension (.06).
Maximum 4 residents per home unless DDA previously approved otherwise, with private bedrooms.
Site addendum DD.ADD.1.0 lists each site, capacity and occupancy date, and includes the Community Settings Rule attestation.
The DDA New Site Visit checklist applies, including proximity to the provider's other sites and heightened scrutiny. OHCQ surveys the site after DDA approval.
Voluntary surrender of the license needs a closure schedule submitted at least 90 days ahead; the Director may require 90 more days of operation (.02F).

policies.title: Regulatory Surveys, Complaint Investigations and Plans of Correction
state_specifics: OHCQ is DDA's monitoring agent. Expect an on-site pre-licensure survey, announced and unannounced visits at least annually, and complaint investigation visits (.04A-D).
Submit the POC at the exit conference or within 10 working days of receiving findings. OHCQ may require it sooner, and its Director may extend up to 30 days (.04E).
If OHCQ rejects a POC, resubmit within 10 working days (.04F).
The governing body approves POC responses (.08C).
OHCQ Developmental Disabilities contacts: 410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220.
Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations start within 2 working days (.03, per research).

policies.title: Conflict of Interest and Fiscal Management
state_specifics: No financial or personal conflict of interest for governing body members, staff, care providers, volunteers and standing committee members (.10A(13)).
Fiscal affairs follow generally accepted accounting practices (.10A(14)).
Board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee (.08C(9)).
Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons may not be paid to provide CL–GH.
Keep individuals' funds separate from agency funds (see IR-05).

policies.title: Fundamental Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: A written policy ensures fundamental rights under Health-General §7-1002 and promotes choice and the exercise of rights (.10A(2)-(3)). Read COMAR 10.22.04.03 and the statute before finalizing the rights list.
Each home must meet HCBS settings conditions: a lease or equivalent agreement, privacy, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, access to food and visitors, and community integration.
The home must not be gated or isolated, and must not sit near the provider's other sites (DDA New Site Visit checklist).
Any modification of a settings condition must follow 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F) and be documented in the person-centered plan.
Train staff on fundamental rights within 3 months of hire (.11D(5)).

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
state_specifics: The standing committee reviews and approves any restriction of a right not related to challenging behavior, and sets its time frame (.14E(1)(e)).
Restrictions tied to behavior require a behavior plan approved by the committee (.14E(1)(d); COMAR 10.22.10).

Federal modification elements: specific assessed need, positive interventions tried, less intrusive methods tried, description of the condition, regular data collection and review, time limits, informed consent, and assurance of no harm.
Individuals receive a right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16 when services are to be terminated (.02G(2)).
Rights restriction records must be in the IP.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Implement a grievance process with safeguards against retaliation for filing (.10A(5)).
Give each individual, and the proponent where appropriate, enough information about the process to use it effectively (.10D).
Provide the process in accessible formats (plain language, pictures, interpretation).
Include an external-contact page listing the DDA regional office and OHCQ (410-402-8100 / 877-402-8220).
The standing committee reviews grievance trends as part of QA.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: A confidentiality policy is required under Health-General §7-1010 (.10A(4)). The standing committee must also keep confidentiality (.14E(7)).
Electronic records must comply with the HIPAA privacy and security rules (.13E(2)(b)).
On a medical emergency, make the person's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel (.13C).
Records stay at the site where the person is served (.13A). Control access to them there.
Designate a privacy officer and a security officer, and include a breach response procedure.

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
state_specifics: A system must ensure funds are used consistent with each person's needs and preferences (.10A(15)(a)).
Keep personal funds separate from agency funds, and transfer them to the individual in a timely manner when services end (.10A(15)(b)).
Individuals have timely access to their funds (.10A(15)(c)) and can request an accounting (.10A(15)(d)).
Interest from an interest-bearing account accrues to the individual's account (.10A(15)(e)).
The licensee's board and staff must have no financial conflict of interest (.10A(13)).
Room and board are collected from the resident, so SSI income ($994/month in 2026 per research) must leave personal spending money.

policies.title: Informed Consent, Proponents and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: COMAR .10A(12) requires the licensee to have a policy complying with Health-General §5-605. Confirm the statute's subject before drafting.
Train staff on supporting individuals and families in making choices (.11D(7)) and on communication skills (.11D(8)).
Informed consent for any rights modification or restrictive technique must be documented in the IP.
Identify each person's proponent or legal decision-maker in the record.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
state_specifics: Services must be provided without discrimination (.10A(6)).
The licensee also needs a separate policy to prevent employment discrimination (.11E(2); see ST-08).
Provide interpreters, accessible formats and assistive communication for individuals and families.
Staff communication-skills training is required within 3 months of hire (.11D(8)).

policies.title: Residency Agreement, Room and Board and Rent
state_specifics: Each resident needs a lease or equivalent legally enforceable residency agreement, with protections against eviction comparable to landlord-tenant law.
Medicaid excludes room and board. Collect it from the resident under a written agreement, and keep it separate from Medicaid billing.
Set an amount residents can afford (2026 federal SSI is $994/month per research).
Residents choose roommates and have private bedrooms, with sharing only by choice, and lockable doors.
Residents control their schedule and have access to food and visitors.

policies.title: Payment for Property Damage
state_specifics: An individual may be required to pay for property damage only if the IP shows all of the following (.10A(11)): a documented history of destructive behavior in the behavior plan, a behavior plan addressing it, ability to pay, approval by the licensee's standing committee, and a report of the approval to the regional director.
Without all five, do not charge the individual.

policies.title: Individuals' Household Tasks and Prohibition on Performing Paid Staff Duties
state_specifics: An individual may not perform the duties of a paid staff person (.10A(18)).
An individual may perform only tasks shared by the household, tasks documented as an activity in the IP, or tasks paid as part of a training program as required by federal or State law (.10A(19)).
Document chore participation in the IP, and pay for any work that is not shared household work.

policies.title: Referral, Admission and Transition In
state_specifics: Referrals and service authorization come through the DDA Regional Office and the person's PCP. Services must be authorized in LTSSMaryland before billing.
At admission, create the record at the site with the items in .13B, including application information, emergency contact, next of kin, physician, diagnosis, allergies and medication list.
Check vacancy and compatibility against the PSP's stated number of individuals per home and the licensed capacity.
Fill vacancies only with DDA authorization; a vacancy changes the billing rate (see GOV-06).

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning and the Individual Plan
state_specifics: The IP is defined in COMAR 10.22.05, and it must be in the record (.13B(3)). Read that chapter and add its timelines before finalizing.
Health and safety needs identified in the IP must be met (.10A(1)).
Staffing levels and patterns come from the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A).
Train staff on individual-directed, outcome-oriented planning within 3 months of hire (.11D(2)).
Services billed must be in the approved PCP.

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: The record must contain documentation demonstrating implementation of the IP (.13B(4)).
Staffing patterns follow the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A).
Daily notes must support each day billed under W5600, and each retainer day.
Document any authorized dedicated hours separately from home staffing.
Hot water above 110°F is allowed only if the IP documents that everyone in the home can regulate temperature safely (.12C).

policies.title: Community Integration, Dedicated Hours and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Train staff on community integration and inclusion within 3 months of hire (.11D(1)).

Dedicated 1:1 hours (W1999) may be shared only for people who are retired, transitioning, recovering, or receiving few day-service hours. Under current text the limit is under 40 hours, and under pending Amendment #4 under 30 hours.
Transportation is included in the daily rate. Use the most cost-effective mode.
Support employment and day-service choices as set out in each PCP, and do not restrict community access without the rights-restriction process (IR-02).

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
state_specifics: Terminate services for good cause only with the Director's written approval (.02G).
Notify the Director in writing 90 days before the proposed termination date (.02G(1)).

Give the individual, and the proponent where appropriate, written notice of the intent to terminate and the right to a hearing under COMAR 10.22.16, within the same 90-day period. Copy the regional office and the individual's team (.02G(2)).
Treat services as terminated after 60 consecutive days of absence unless the Director decides otherwise (.02G(3)).
Transfer personal funds to the individual in a timely manner when services end (.10A(15)(b)).
Keep the record at least 6 years after services end (.13D(1)).

policies.title: Medication Administration and Medication Technician Certification
state_specifics: Administer all medication per DDA's curriculum on medication training (.10A(8); .12D(1)).
Unlicensed staff who give medication or treatments must be Maryland Board of Nursing certified Medication Technicians working under RN delegation (waiver standard).
Medication administration training is required before independent duties (.11C(2)(d)).
Oral solid medication comes in unit-dose packages unless the IP says otherwise (.12D(2)). Send medication for an absent person in a separate, easily identified pharmaceutical package (.12D(3)).
Request computer-generated MARs, TARs and physician order forms from the pharmacy (.12D(4)).
Keep the allergy list and medication list in the record (.13B(2)(e)-(f)).

policies.title: Delegating Nurse Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: Have a policy ensuring compliance with COMAR 10.27.11, Delegation of Nursing Functions (.10A(9)). Read that chapter before finalizing.
The waiver standard requires RN delegation of nursing tasks to unlicensed staff.
Nursing Support Services are included within CL–GH based on assessed need; the Regional Office may authorize additional standalone hours after a health change or hospital discharge.
Document the individual's physician, diagnosis and medication list in the record (.13B(2)).

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Health and safety needs identified in the IP must be met (.10A(1)).
Seizure disorders training is required before independent duties (.11C(2)(a)).
Include aging-process training (.11C(2)(e)) and First Aid/CPR within 3 months of hire (.11D(4)); the waiver standard requires CPR/First Aid with an in-person skills check.
Record diagnoses and allergies per .13B(2).
Choking-risk protocols belong in the IP and are not set by a specific COMAR section (none found in the sections fetched).

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: On notification of a medical emergency, make the individual's medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel (.13C).
Incidents involving life-threatening conditions must be reported and investigated under DDA procedures (.10A(7)).
The QA system must respond promptly and appropriately when an individual's health or safety is at risk (.14B(5)).
Keep emergency contact, next of kin and physician in each record (.13B(2)).

policies.title: Death of an Individual
state_specifics: Report a death under DDA procedures on reportable incidents (.10A(7)). Insert the current PORII reporting level and deadline; those were not verified here.
Keep the record at least 6 years after a person dies (.13D(1)).
The standing committee reviews all incidents (.14E(1)(c)).
Return personal funds and property in a timely manner (.10A(15)(b)).
Notify family or the proponent and the DDA regional office.

policies.title: Positive Behavior Support and Behavior Plans
state_specifics: A policy must ensure that an individual whose behavior requires intervention receives the safeguards required by the chapter (.10A(10)).
Behavior plans that use restrictive techniques must be approved by the standing committee and comply with COMAR 10.22.04.03A and 10.22.10 (.14E(1)(d)).
Training on principles of behavior change and management of disruptive behaviors is required before independent duties (.11C(2)(b)-(c)).
COMAR 10.22.10.05 covers the Behavior Plan; its text was not read.

policies.title: Restrictive Interventions, Restraint and Seclusion
state_specifics: COMAR 10.22.10 has separate sections on Use of Restrictive Techniques (.06), Physical Restraint (.08), Mechanical Restraint and Support (.09) and Chemical Restraint (.10). Their text was not read; copy permitted techniques, limits and documentation from them before finalizing.
Track each use: individual, technique, date and time, emergency vs. plan, effectiveness (.14B(4)).
The standing committee approves all behavior plans using restrictive techniques (.14E(1)(d)).
Seclusion: check the 10.22.10 text on whether it is addressed, and do not state a rule here that is unverified.

policies.title: Medications Used to Modify Behavior and Restrictive Technique Monitoring
state_specifics: COMAR 10.22.10.07 covers Use of Medications to Modify Challenging Behavior, and .11 covers Monitoring Use of Medications to Modify Behavior and Restrictive Techniques. Their text was not read.
The QA system must record the medication or technique, date and time, whether emergency or planned, and whether it meets behavior plan goals (.14B(4)).
The standing committee reviews trends.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: All incidents must be reported and investigated per DDA procedures (.10A(7)). Use the current DDA PORII for abuse, neglect and exploitation categories and deadlines (not verified here).
Mandatory-reporter duties under Family Law §14-302 for vulnerable adults were not verified; confirm before use.
Reports are made to the local department of social services (Adult Protective Services), and to DDA and OHCQ per PORII.
Do not retaliate against anyone who reports (see the anti-retaliation safeguard in .10A(5)).
Background checks bar anyone whose history shows behavior potentially harmful to individuals (.11B).

policies.title: Reportable Incidents and Investigations
state_specifics: Report and investigate all incidents, including life-threatening conditions, per DDA's procedures on reportable incidents (.10A(7)). Insert PORII levels, deadlines and forms from the current policy; these were not verified here.
The standing committee reviews the incident protocol and all incidents to identify deficient practices and recommend corrective action (.14E(1)(b)-(c)).
OHCQ conducts complaint and incident investigations. Priority 1 investigations start within 2 working days (.03, per research).
POC due at the exit conference or within 10 working days (.04E).

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
state_specifics: A missing person is a reportable incident under the DDA procedure (.10A(7)). Insert the PORII category and deadline once verified.
Include search steps, police notification, and notification of the proponent and DDA regional office.
Individuals' IPs must address elopement risk (.10A(1)).
The standing committee reviews every incident (.14E(1)(c)).

policies.title: Residential Environment and Accessibility
state_specifics: Each home must meet local zoning (except as in Health-General §7-603), local and State building requirements and life-safety requirements. It must be free of hazards and in good repair (.12A).
Water at a maximum of 110°F unless every resident can regulate it safely and the IP documents it (.12C).
Maximum 4 residents, each with a private bedroom (sharing only by choice), and lockable bedroom doors.
Site addendum DD.ADD.1.0 asks whether the site is wheelchair accessible. Plan for accessibility based on residents' needs.
The home must not be gated or isolated from the community.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drills
state_specifics: A written fire evacuation plan is required, with adequate smoke detectors and working, updated fire extinguishers (.12B).
An effective disaster and emergency evacuation plan with sufficient evacuation drills is required (.10A(17)). COMAR sets no drill frequency in the text fetched; confirm with the local fire marshal.

Emergency plan for all emergencies and disasters (.10B): procedures before, during and after; evacuation or 72-hour shelter-in-place; annual practice drill coordinated with local emergency planners; after-action report and improvement plan; ID with health and contact information; role of resident, family and legal representative; and medical needs at shelters.

Also include notification of families, staff and the DDA regional office; staff coverage and recall; continuity of operations; off-site backup of records; sharing the plan with local emergency management; and an executive summary for families on request.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: State and federally required safety precautions, infection control and standard precautions must be implemented (.10A(16)).
Blood-borne pathogens training under 29 CFR 1910.1030 is required before independent duties (.11C(3)).
Communicable diseases training is required within 3 months of hire (.11D(6)).
Maintain a written OSHA exposure control plan, offer hepatitis B vaccination, and provide annual bloodborne pathogen training.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Residents must have access to food at any time. Any restriction needs an IP-documented modification.
Record allergies and diagnoses (.13B(2)).
Diet orders and modified textures must be in the IP and follow physician orders. No COMAR section on diets was found in the sections fetched.

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Transportation is included in the daily rate. Use the most cost-effective mode.
Staff who drive need a valid driver's license, and all vehicles must be insured.
Include auto insurance documentation (DDA application Attachment 12).
Maintain emergency information and medication plans for outings, and transport only per the IP.

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Supervision and Overnight Coverage
state_specifics: Maryland sets no fixed staff ratio. The licensee analyzes the number and needs of individuals served and develops and implements a staffing plan that meets health and safety needs and IP services (.11A).
Staffing levels and patterns follow the IP (COMAR 10.22.08.04A).
Services must be available 24/7 at each licensed site, with back-up and emergency support.
DDA's rate assumes 43.14 staff-hours per day for a 4-person home with overnight supervision (research S10); use it as a planning benchmark only.
Overnight coverage (awake or asleep) is set by each person's assessed needs and the IP; COMAR does not mandate awake overnight staff in the sections fetched.
Any person who meets the training requirements and has no disqualifying criminal history may be on the staffing plan (.11A).

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Do not employ or contract with anyone whose criminal history indicates behavior potentially harmful to individuals, documented through a criminal history records check or background check (.11B).
Cite Health-General §19-1902 et seq. and COMAR 12.15.03 (statute text not verified).
Check every staff member, contractor and volunteer before direct contact. Record on the DDA Staff Criminal History form.
Screen against the OIG LEIE and the Maryland sanctioned provider list.
Fingerprint checks run through CJIS using DDA's agency authorization codes in the DDA instructions.

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Pre-Service Training
state_specifics: Before independent duties, document that all staff and care providers (.11C): receive adequate job training; complete DDA-approved training on seizure disorders, principles of behavior change, management of disruptive behaviors, medication administration, and the aging process; and receive blood-borne pathogens training per 29 CFR 1910.1030.
Document on the DDA Staff Training form DD.APP.1.1.
No unsupervised duties until the pre-service training record is signed off.

policies.title: Three-Month Training Requirements, CPR and First Aid
state_specifics: Within 3 months of hire, complete DDA-approved training on (.11D): community integration and inclusion; individual-directed outcome-oriented planning; general characteristics and needs of individuals served; First Aid and CPR (American Red Cross or equivalent); fundamental rights; communicable diseases; supporting choices; and communication skills.
Waiver standard: First Aid/CPR with an in-person skills check for all direct staff.
Record on DD.APP.1.1.

policies.title: Employee Health, Communicable Disease and TB Screening
state_specifics: COMAR 10.22.02 in the sections fetched sets no TB-testing mandate. This policy is based on the infection-control duty in .10A(16) and communicable diseases training in .11D(6).
Set pre-employment health screening and TB screening by agency policy, following local health department guidance.
Offer hepatitis B vaccination under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030.
Exclude ill staff from work when they could transmit communicable disease.

policies.title: Personnel Records and Job Descriptions
state_specifics: Each position has a written job description including the nature and extent of training and experience required (.11E(1)).
Each personnel file holds the criminal history check result, training documentation (DD.APP.1.1), license or certification (e.g., Medication Technician, CPR), and exclusion screening.
Training must be documented to show it was completed before independent duties (.11C).
Retention periods for personnel files are not set in the COMAR sections fetched; adopt a period of at least 6 years consistent with .13D.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No financial or personal conflict of interest for staff, care providers and volunteers (.10A(13)).
Relatives, legal guardians and legally responsible persons may not be paid to provide CL–GH.
No borrowing from, or financial dealings with, individuals served; follow the personal funds policy (IR-05).
Staff must implement every policy as adopted (.10C).

policies.title: Employment Nondiscrimination
state_specifics: A policy to prevent employment discrimination is required (.11E(2)).
Pair with the written job descriptions (.11E(1)).

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Leave Compliance
state_specifics: State minimum wage is $15.00/hr. Montgomery County is $18.00 (51+ employees), $16.50 (11–50, and certain nonprofits and Medicaid-funded home care providers) and $15.95 (10 or fewer). Howard County is $16.00. Prince George's County is $15.30 (as of July 1, 2026).
Earned sick and safe leave accrues at 1 hour per 30 worked, up to 40 hours per year, and is paid when the employer has 15 or more employees (§3-1304).
FAMLI contributions start January 1, 2027 at 0.9% of wages, split 0.45% employer / 0.45% employee; employers under 15 employees remit only the employee share (research S63).
Pay overtime per FLSA; treat paid training time as hours worked.

policies.title: Volunteers, Contractors and Consultants
state_specifics: Volunteers, consultants and contractors must be aware of and follow all policies (.10C).
Background checks apply to anyone the licensee employs or contracts with (.11B).
Volunteers and care providers receive the same pre-service and 3-month training as staff (.11C-D).
No conflict of interest for volunteers (.10A(13)).

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep each individual's records at the site where the person is served (.13A).

Minimum contents: application identifying information; emergency contact; next of kin; physician; diagnosis; allergies; medication list; the IP; documentation of IP implementation; and anything else DDA requires (.13B).
Make medical information readily accessible to emergency personnel (.13C).

Retain records at least 6 years, even if the person no longer receives services or dies. Keep documents relevant to current services as long as the person is served, and organize for easy access (.13D).

policies.title: Electronic Records, Backup and Security
state_specifics: Electronic records are encouraged (.13E(1)).
They must meet the chapter, comply with the HIPAA privacy and security rules, and be properly backed up and stored off-site (.13E(2)).

The emergency plan must back up and electronically store off-site appropriate records of individuals, staff and facility documents, with an electronic copy of the emergency plan available on request from emergency management organizations (.10B(5)).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Incident reports go to DDA under PORII (deadlines to be inserted from the current policy).
POC to OHCQ within 10 working days of findings (.04E).
Report approval of a property-damage payment to the regional director (.10A(11)(e)).
Notify DDA regional office when the emergency plan is activated (.10B(2)).
Submit revised PSP and QA plan changes for DDA approval (.09B; .14A).
Give the Director 90 days' notice of terminating services (.02G) or surrendering the license (.02F).
Submit license renewal at least 60 days before expiration (.02B).
Notify DDA at least 30 days ahead of a site opening, closure or relocation (.05).
